notes.meaning: John the Baptist's followers came and gave his body an honorable burial in a tomb. They showed deep loyalty to their teacher even after his violent death at the hands of King Herod. Then they went to Jesus to bring Him the sad news.

The twelve apostles returned to Jesus after being sent out across the towns to preach and heal. They gathered around Him and gave a full report of everything they had done and taught during their trip. Jesus listened carefully to all they had experienced.

Jesus told His tired disciples to come away with Him to a quiet place so they could get some rest. Great crowds were continually coming and going, leaving them without even enough time to sit down and eat a meal. Jesus showed tender care for their physical and spiritual needs.
Jesus and the disciples got into a boat to cross to a remote spot by themselves. They hoped to find a quiet place away from the busy crowds.
Many people saw the boat leaving and recognized Jesus and the apostles. Crowds from all the nearby towns ran along the shore on foot and got to the landing place before the boat arrived.

When Jesus stepped ashore, He saw a huge crowd waiting for Him. Instead of being annoyed by the loss of rest, He felt deep pity for them because their religious leaders had left them like sheep without a shepherd. He immediately began to teach them God's truth.

Late in the afternoon, the disciples came to Jesus and pointed out how desolate the area was. They urged Him to dismiss the crowd so the people could reach nearby farms and villages to buy food before sunset.

Jesus challenged the disciples by telling them to feed the crowd themselves. Surprised, they asked if they were expected to spend two hundred silver coins—about eight months of a laborer's wages—to buy enough bread for so many people.
Jesus told the disciples to go find out what food was already available. After checking among the people, they reported that they had only five small loaves of bread and two fish.

Jesus directed everyone to sit down in groups on the green spring grass. They sat in orderly rows of fifties and hundreds, looking like neat garden beds. This made it easy to count the crowd and made sure no one was missed when the food was distributed.

Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up toward heaven, and praised God. As He broke the loaves, the food multiplied in His hands, and He kept handing the pieces to the disciples to distribute. He also divided the two fish so that everyone received some.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The actions of taking, blessing, breaking, and giving the bread point forward to the Eucharist (the Lord's Supper), where Christ gives His own body as spiritual food.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teach that no supernatural multiplication happened, but rather that Jesus inspired the people in the crowd to share the food they had brought with them.

notes.meaning: Every person in the vast crowd ate and was completely satisfied. Jesus gave them more than enough food to meet their hunger.
The disciples gathered up twelve large baskets full of leftover pieces of bread and fish. These leftovers showed the greatness of the miracle and taught that God's gifts should never be wasted.
The total number of adult men who ate the meal was about five thousand, not counting the women and children with them. Feeding such a massive gathering proved Jesus' divine power over nature.
Immediately after the meal, Jesus urged His disciples to get into the boat and sail ahead of Him toward Bethsaida. He wanted them away from the excited crowd so He could dismiss the people Himself.
After sending the crowd away, Jesus went up on a mountainside alone to pray. He made time with His Heavenly Father a priority, even after an exhausting day of ministry.
As night fell, the disciples were far out in the middle of the lake while Jesus was alone on the land. A strong contrary wind made their crossing dangerous and difficult.

Jesus saw His disciples struggling hard at the oars against the heavy wind. Late in the night, between three and six in the morning, He came walking on the water toward them, revealing His divine power as Lord of creation.

When the disciples saw someone walking on the lake, they cried out in panic, thinking it was a ghost. Jesus immediately spoke to them, telling them to take courage and not be afraid because it was Him.
Jesus climbed into the boat with the disciples, and the wind instantly died down. The disciples were completely stunned and filled with awe at what they had just seen.

The disciples were so shocked because they had not truly understood the miracle of the bread from earlier that day. Their minds were dull and their hearts were slow to recognize Jesus' divine authority.
They crossed the lake, landed at the fertile plain of Gennesaret, and tied up the boat. The rough night wind had blown them slightly off their original course.

As soon as Jesus and the disciples stepped onto the shore, the local people recognized Him. News traveled rapidly, and people ran across the region carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.

Wherever Jesus went—in villages, towns, or country markets—people brought the sick out into public places. They begged simply to touch the edge of His robe, and every person who touched Him was fully healed.
